findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are stored in plain text in the Lambda function's environment variables, readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration and committed to source control.

The Lambda environment variables are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (no kms_key_arn set), so sensitive values rely only on the service default key and are exposed in the console/API in plaintext.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS.
No vpc_config is specified, so the function runs outside a VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no network-layer egress controls, providing a data exfiltration path.
The function has no code_signing_config_arn, so deployment packages are not signature-validated and tampering between build and deployment would go undetected.
The Lambda execution role is created without a permissions_boundary, so there is no guardrail limiting the maximum privileges that can be attached to this role.
